gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Macworld ran a one-hour Blackmagic test on the OWC Express 1M2 (Thomas Bergbold, Aug 19 2024): the transfer rate did not drop and the case reached about 40 °C. Hardware Busters ran a 15-minute stress test on the TerraMaster D1 SSD Plus in a 30 °C room (Sep 4 2025) and saw no thermal throttling, with a 54.8 °C maximum.
standout_why: I compared against four pages. itechguides.com (cited) gives only OWC's and Satechi's own speed figures, no temperatures and no throttling data. It says only that a drive 'may eventually throttle'. soldermag.com (rank 5) has no measurements at all and calls the OWC Express 1M2 'poor thermal performance' without a test behind it. ChatGPT's own answer says the OWC's 'independent extended-write results are mixed', and our current page cites only a vendor blog claiming 'moderate to severe throttling' for it. I also tried the cited Tom's Hardware best-picks page (dated 2022-11-18), but it would not load beyond its title, so I could not check it. None of these pages names a long-duration test with a duration, a temperature and a result for the OWC 1M2 or the D1 SSD Plus. ChatGPT got PCWorld's 450 GB CM642 result through our page, so that one is not new.
decides: The finding backs the passive pick: the OWC Express 1M2 (one hour, no speed drop, about 40 °C) and the TerraMaster D1 SSD Plus (15 minutes at 30 °C ambient, no throttling, 54.8 °C maximum; NAS Compares 2,550–2,600 MB/s write in an AJA loop) both have named long-run tests with no throttling. That undercuts the 'mixed' and 'poor thermal' claims. The fan pick, the UGREEN CM642, still has PCWorld's 450 GB write with no thermal issues. Its sibling the CM850 lost the drive during that same write with its sleeve on, which shows enclosure cooling matters on the same chip. The page can then say that the one named failure under a long load went to the sleeved CM850 and the passive ZIKE Z666. The finned OWC and TerraMaster bodies and the fan-cooled CM642 held up in every named test.

findings.label: One-hour sustained transfer: did speed drop
findings.value: No drop in transfer rate after 1 hour
findings.note: Thomas Bergbold for Macwelt, translated by Roman Loyola. Published Aug 19, 2024. Blackmagic Disk Speed Test run for about one hour. The article gives no MB/s figure for the long run and does not name the SSD inside the fully configured unit.

findings.label: Case temperature after 1 hour of load
findings.note: Same run. The fins and underside were 'noticeably warm' at 30 minutes. The measuring method is not stated.

findings.label: AJA System Test Lite (short run)
findings.note: Macworld, Aug 19 2024. A burst benchmark, not a sustained one.

findings.label: 15-minute sustained stress test: max temperature and throttling
findings.value: 54.8 °C maximum, about 55 °C plateau, no thermal throttling
findings.source_title: TerraMaster D1 SSD Plus 40Gbps NVMe Enclosure Review, page 4 (Hardware Busters)
findings.note: Hardware Busters, Sep 4 2025. CrystalDiskMark looped for 15 minutes in a 30 °C room. Idle was about 36 °C and normal loads about 42–44 °C. IR readings were 55.2, 51.7 and 54.8 °C. The page names neither the SSD nor the host, and gives no MB/s for the stress run.

findings.label: Sustained AJA 1 GB loop write, and temperatures after more than 5 minutes of large-file writes
findings.value: 2,550–2,600 MB/s write (3,000–3,100 MB/s read), no throttling; SSD 44–45 °C, enclosure 41–42 °C
findings.source_title: Terramaster D1 SSD Review – Performance Made Sustainable? (NAS Compares)
findings.note: Rob Andrews, NAS Compares. The page shows only '1 year ago', no exact date. The SSD is an unnamed PCIe Gen4 x4 drive. A 100 GB mixed-content transfer took 63 s at an average of 1,580 MB/s.

findings.label: SSD temperature at the end of a near-full 1.9 TB write
findings.value: 73 (unit not printed; presumably °C), falling to 60 in under a minute
findings.source_title: TerraMaster D1 Plus Portable SSD Enclosure Review (Gizmochina)
findings.note: Alex Su, Gizmochina, Jul 28 2025. Ambient was 27 (room temperature). The SSD was an unnamed Gen4 drive. The review gives no MB/s over time and does not say whether the drive throttled. The case temperature kept rising for the whole run.

findings.label: 450 GB write vs UGREEN CM850 with the same SSD
findings.value: D1 won the 450 GB write ('a major win'); no figure printed in the text
findings.source_title: TerraMaster D1 SSD Plus enclosure review (PCWorld)
findings.note: Jon L. Jacobi, Aug 20 2025. Both enclosures used a Samsung 9100 Pro 4TB on a Z890 test bed. The numbers are only in chart images. Price when reviewed: $109.99.

findings.label: 450 GB write
findings.value: Completed with no thermal issues; fastest unpopulated USB4 enclosure PCWorld had tested
findings.note: Jon L. Jacobi, Feb 11 2025. 8TB WD SN850X on an i5-12400 / Z790 Thunderbolt 4 test bed. The times are only in charts. The text says the 450 GB time was slower than a couple of 20 Gbps USB 3.2x2 SSDs. Price when reviewed: $110.

findings.label: Temperature under benchmark load, and large-file copy
findings.value: 26 °C idle → 34 °C → 43 °C, then stable; copy averaged 650 MB/s write and 980 MB/s read
findings.source_title: Test UGREEN CM642 – Un boitier pour SSD NVMe compatible USB4 (IT-Connect)
findings.note: Florian Burnel, May 1 2024. Samsung 990 Pro in a Geekom IT13 (USB4). The copy size and the temperature method are not stated. Commenters point out that 650/980 MB/s looks like USB 3.2 speed, so don't use the copy figure as a USB4 result.

findings.label: Case temperature after 10–15 minutes of work
findings.source_title: Ugreen M2 CM642 NVMe SSD Pocket Review: Speed and Protection (hi-tech.ua)
findings.note: Andrew Writter, Jul 22 2024. Measured in summer heat. The workload, SSD and ambient temperature are not stated. Weak evidence.

findings.label: 450 GB write with the silicone sleeve on
findings.value: The drive disappeared mid-write; the write finished with the sleeve off or a fan over it
findings.note: Jon L. Jacobi, Feb 7 2025. 8TB WD SN850X on PCWorld's Thunderbolt 4 test bed. The author attributes it to 'no doubt' thermal issues. Same ASM2464PD chip as the CM642. Price when reviewed: $89.99.

findings.label: CrystalDiskMark SEQ1M Q8T1 on USB4, and long write
findings.value: 3,268.40 MB/s write, 3,363.08 MB/s read; about 600 GB written 'past saturation'
findings.source_title: Unitek SolidForce Reefer TurboCool USB4 M.2 SSD Enclosure Review: 40Gbps With a Fan (Back2Gaming)
findings.note: BossMac Suba, last updated Oct 8 2026. Kingston NV3 2TB on a Ryzen 9 9950X. Room temperature was 28 °C. The review gives no MB/s over time and no drive temperature. Price stated: $92.99 at the Unitek store.

findings.product: ZIKE Z666 vs ACASIS TBU405 Pro M1
findings.label: Write stress test of more than 50 minutes
findings.value: The ZIKE Z666 (passive) overheated; the ACASIS TBU405 Pro M1 (fan) did not
findings.source_title: ZIKE VS ACASIS Thermal Throttling Stress Test Thunderbolt USB4 SSD Enclosures - Apple Silicon M4 Mac
findings.note: David Harry's video, published Dec 23 2025, reposted on this page. WD SN850X 4TB in both enclosures on an Apple Silicon M4 Mac, measured with Blackmagic before and after. No MB/s or temperature figures are given.

unsourced: Exact 48 GB and 450 GB copy times or MB/s for the UGREEN CM642, CM850 and TerraMaster D1 SSD Plus. PCWorld and Macworld put them only in chart images, and the text has no numbers.
